name: riven
description: Read your Riven Apple Watch strength workouts: every set's exercise, reps and muscle failure score.

interface.longDescription:
Riven is automatic exercise tracking and muscle failure detection on the Apple Watch. During a strength workout the watch detects each set, names the exercise, logs the reps and scores how close every set came to true muscle failure, from 0 to 100 %. No barbell clip, no camera, no manual logging.

Connect Riven and ask your assistant about your training in plain language:
- "Which muscles did I actually train to failure this week?"
- "Show me every workout from October, set by set."
- "My chest sets keep stopping short. What should I change on Thursday?"
- "How has my lat pulldown changed this month?"
- "Compare this week with last week and plan next week around what I skipped."

What the assistant can read (read-only):
- Every workout with its full per-set breakdown: exercise, muscle group, reps, failure % and verdict
- Workout overviews, weekly summaries and this-week-vs-last-week comparisons
- Muscle failure by muscle group, so you can see which muscles get enough hard sets
- Progress on any single exercise over time

The failure score: 90 % and above means the set reached muscle failure, the point that drives muscle growth; 75–89 % near failure; 50–74 % working; under 50 % stopped short.

Privacy: the connection is read-only and shares only workouts. Never heart rate, sensor data, Apple Health data, your name or your email. You sign in with Apple and approve the connection yourself, and you can disconnect at any time.

Requirements: the Riven app on iPhone and Apple Watch, signed in with Apple (Settings → Profile → Sign in with Apple).
capabilities: Every workout with a per-set breakdown
defaultPrompt: Which muscles did I train to failure this week?
Show me my last workout set by set
Compare this week with last week

positive.prompt: Show me all my Riven workouts with every set.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_all_workouts (following next_cursor until null) and lists each workout with its sets: exercise, reps and failure %.

positive.prompt: Which muscles did I train to failure in the last 4 weeks?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls failure_by_muscle and reports per muscle group the sets that reached failure (90%+) and the average failure %.

positive.prompt: How did this week of training compare with last week?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls weekly_summary and compares workouts, sets, reps, sets at failure and average failure % between the two weeks.

positive.prompt: How has my bench press changed over the last month?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls exercise_history with 'bench press' and summarises reps and failure % per session over time.

positive.prompt: Break down my last workout set by set.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_workouts to find the most recent workout, then get_workout, and lists every set with exercise, reps and failure verdict.

negative.prompt: What's the weather in Madrid tomorrow?

negative.description: Asks to change data (tools are read-only)
negative.prompt: Delete my workout from yesterday in Riven.
Based on my heart rate, do I have a heart condition?
